reasons.action: The brief explicitly requests a performed behavior — a bricklayer laying a course, one brick per hit — so the action is request-governed; the only supplied reference is audio and cannot author a visual action.
reasons.medium: No visual reference exists (the sole asset is an audio beat), so no reference medium has authority; the medium owner is fixed by the accepted medium_decision and no reference may claim it.
reasons.wardrobe: With no visual reference present, no observed clothing exists to inherit; wardrobe therefore falls to the request, which names a bricklayer without contradicting any source attire.
reasons.lighting: The lighting is not described by any reference — an audio kick pattern carries no illuminant, direction or quality — and no director note addresses it, so lighting is request-governed.
reasons.framing: The brief states no camera composition, shot scale or viewpoint, and the aspect ratio alone is not a framing instruction; with no visual reference to observe, framing remains request-governed rather than reference- or metadata-derived.
reasons.palette: No reference grades or colors the image and no director note sets a treatment, so the scene's tonal and color handling is request-governed by default.
